ci_support_linux_64_.yaml:
DOCKER_PLATFORM:
- linux/amd64
channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
ttl3d turns RDF (Turtle, N-Triples, RDF/XML, JSON-LD, TriG, N-Quads), a SPARQL CONSTRUCT or
DESCRIBE result, or tables (CSV/TSV files, pandas DataFrames) into a single self-contained HTML
page that shows the graph in 3D or 2D, with a legend, label search and a detail card per node.
The page inlines all of its JavaScript (a bundle of three.js and force-graph, whose licenses ship
in ttl3d/vendor/LICENSES.md), so it opens from disk and works offline. A Python API shows the
same page inline in Jupyter. Release notes: https://github.com/soheilabadifard/TTL_to_3D/releases
about.summary: Turn RDF graphs, SPARQL results and tables into a self-contained, offline 2D/3D HTML viewer

script: python -c "from pathlib import Path; assert '<title>tiny</title>' in Path('page.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')"

name: ttl3d
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.9.2"

package:
  name: ttl3d
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/t/ttl3d/ttl3d-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 712786cb7347a0261002c1f90cc457583a49f28dfdff237fbcfa7724296a034a

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv
  python:
    entry_points:
      - ttl3d = ttl3d.cli:main

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    - setuptools >=68
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    - rdflib >=7
    - networkx >=3
    - numpy
    - scipy

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - ttl3d
      pip_check: true
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
  - requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    script:
      - ttl3d --version
      - python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('tiny.ttl').write_text('<http://example.org/a> <http://example.org/p> <http://example.org/b> .', encoding='utf-8')"
      - ttl3d tiny.ttl -o page.html
      - python -c "from pathlib import Path; assert '<title>tiny</title>' in Path('page.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')"

about:
  homepage: https://soheilabadifard.github.io/TTL_to_3D/
  repository: https://github.com/soheilabadifard/TTL_to_3D
  documentation: https://soheilabadifard.github.io/TTL_to_3D/tutorial.html
  summary: Turn RDF graphs, SPARQL results and tables into a self-contained, offline 2D/3D HTML viewer
  description: |
    ttl3d turns RDF (Turtle, N-Triples, RDF/XML, JSON-LD, TriG, N-Quads), a SPARQL CONSTRUCT or
    DESCRIBE result, or tables (CSV/TSV files, pandas DataFrames) into a single self-contained HTML
    page that shows the graph in 3D or 2D, with a legend, label search and a detail card per node.
    The page inlines all of its JavaScript (a bundle of three.js and force-graph, whose licenses ship
    in ttl3d/vendor/LICENSES.md), so it opens from disk and works offline. A Python API shows the
    same page inline in Jupyter. Release notes: https://github.com/soheilabadifard/TTL_to_3D/releases
  license: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - ttl3d/vendor/LICENSES.md

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - soheilabadifard
